business: Moduo: an all-in-one workspace (tasks, notes, calendar, contacts, email), pitched as a client hub for solo service businesses
by_segment: Solo founder of a small service business
why_not: Spark, Todoist and Calendly already work fine together for me, and I've paid for them. This would mean moving my whole setup over, and it still doesn't touch invoicing, which is the part of my month I actually hate.
I already pay for Spark, Todoist and Calendly and they work fine together for me. Moving all my client email into another company's cloud to save a few clicks isn't worth tearing up a setup I trust.

My email runs on Outlook / Microsoft 365, and they say outright that Outlook isn't supported yet. The whole pitch is turning emails into tasks so I don't lose follow-ups, and that doesn't work for me at all.

My clients, contracts and invoices already live in HoneyBook and my hours in Toggl, and this doesn't do either, so it would be one more app next to them, not one fewer. I might poke at the free plan, but I wouldn't pay $12 a month on top of what I already pay.

I'd probably start the no-card trial on day one because that's what I do, but I wouldn't pay. Nothing here tells me where my clients' email ends up, and I've dropped every all-in-one app I've tried within a few weeks anyway.

My whole business runs out of my Gmail stars and flags, and I'm not moving that into an app from a company I've never heard of that could fold next year. Maybe I'd poke at the free plan, but I wouldn't pay $12 a month on what I earn just to replace a habit that mostly works.

I'd maybe poke at the free trial, but I already know how this ends: the email side won't be as good as my real client, so I'd keep that open anyway and this becomes one more tab I pay for. Anything I don't open every week gets cut at my next audit, and I don't see this replacing what I already use.

My current mess of apps works well enough, and I've got five clients plus two proposals out, so there's no weekend free to move everything over. A 14-day trial won't help if I can't even find the time to set it up properly.

My whole client life runs through Outlook on Microsoft 365, and it says right there that Outlook email isn't supported yet, so the email-to-task part that would have saved me last month just doesn't work for me. Without the email, it's one more app next to my Notion setup, not instead of it.
flip: If it turned the time and tasks I log against a client into an invoice at the end of the month, so I could drop the spreadsheet.
A clear promise that my email stays on my machine or is encrypted so the company can't read it, and then the client view actually saving me time every morning past the second week.
Proper Outlook / Microsoft 365 support for email and calendar, plus a few months of independent reviews saying it doesn't drop or mangle email.
Seeing that the email part is good enough that I could actually quit my current mail client and calendar app, so it replaces subscriptions instead of adding one.
A clear local-only or end-to-end encrypted option for email, so my client mail never sits on Moduo's servers.
If it clearly replaced Spark and Todoist so my total bill went down, and I could try it on one real client for the free trial without moving everything over.
If it handled invoices and time tracking well enough that I could cancel HoneyBook and Toggl, so it saves me money instead of adding a subscription.

Seeing it work inside my existing Gmail flow, so starring an email or replying automatically lands the follow-up on the right client without me switching apps, and a friend freelancer saying it actually stopped them dropping follow-ups.
A one-click import from Todoist and my client spreadsheet that has me running in under an hour, plus it replacing Calendly so I'm actually cutting a subscription, not adding one.
Seeing another freelancer I trust use it for a year without problems, and it reminding me about follow-ups I forgot right inside my email without me changing how I work.
If it imported my Notion client pages and let me track hours and invoice clients from the client view, so it could replace the spreadsheet too.
If it pulled in my existing Gmail, calendar and contacts on its own and had my clients set up within an hour, so I wasn't moving anything by hand.
If after two weeks the client view had really saved me from digging through four apps before a client call, and I could cancel my separate task and notes apps so it doesn't cost me more overall.
Built-in time tracking and invoicing tied to each client, so I could cancel Toggl and my invoicing tool and come out even or ahead.
A good number of independent reviews and Reddit threads from consultants who've used it for six months or more saying the Gmail and calendar sync is solid.
If it could import my Notion client pages and the email side was genuinely good enough to drop my mail client, so the follow-up reminders actually live where I read mail.
If I could keep my own email client and just have Moduo pull in each client's emails, tasks and meetings automatically, with an easy import from my Notion setup, I might try the free plan.
If it could pull in my existing inbox and calendar and build the client view for me in under an hour, so the dropped follow-ups show up without me re-entering anything.
If it tracked time against a client and turned those hours into an invoice at the end of the month, so I could cancel Bonsai and Toggl.
Full Outlook / Microsoft 365 email and calendar support, plus a way to bring my clients and notes over from Notion.
